body:
Closes #31.

## What the issue asked for

> Привет / Тебе или твоим друзьям … — Здравствуйте / Вам или вашим друзьям … It is also important to understand what was used more in our dialog ("ты" or "вы") automatically using regexes or peg grammars or similar. May be we can even use our rules or context discovery rules. Not talking for long means at least 90 days not talking. Also we need to make sure we have safe or debug mode, where we only pre-fill one message at a time and user sends it after confirmation.

## What this PR adds

**1. ты/вы detection** (`js/src/crm/address-form.js`) is built on a data table of word-level regex rules. Word boundaries are Unicode-aware because `\b` only knows ASCII, so "ты" never fires inside "работы" and "вы" never fires inside "выход".
- The rules cover Russian pronouns, possessives and verbs, plus Chinese 你/您 and Hindi तुम/आप.
- The owner's own messages count twice.
- The result explains itself: the form, a reason (`majority` / `tie` / `no-evidence`), a confidence and the rules that fired.
- A tie or no evidence falls back to the polite "вы".
- To use **our own rules**, add a `pattern:*` link labelled `address:informal` or `address:formal`; it becomes an extra rule.

**2. Dormant contacts and a safe session** (`js/src/crm/reengage.js`):
- **Finding contacts:** 1:1 chats with no message for at least **90 days**; groups, channels and bots are excluded, and the owner must have written there at least once.
- **Default texts:** the two texts from the issue, replaceable with `--informal`, `--formal`, `--templates` and `{name}`.
- **Safe mode (alias `debug`) is the default.** One prefilled draft at a time is sent only on `confirm()`, and `sendAll()` throws `SafeModeError`. A failed send keeps the draft current.
- **No repeats:** every decision is stored as a `reengage:<source>:<chat>` link, so nobody is offered again until the threshold passes again.

**3. Three surfaces over the same core:**
- **CLI:**
  - `meta-sovereign reengage` previews the plan.
  - `--interactive` asks for each draft: `y` send, `m` I sent it myself, `e` edit, `f` switch ты/вы, `s` skip, `q` quit.
  - `--mode=batch` refuses to run without `--confirm=true`.
- **HTTP:**
  - `POST /api/reengage/plan`.
  - `/send` needs `confirm: true`; a failed send returns 502.
  - `/mark`.
  - `/run` needs `mode: "batch"` and `confirm: true`.
- **SPA — the new Re-engage screen:**
  - One editable draft at a time, with the detected form and its evidence.
  - **Switch to formal/informal**, **Send**, **Copy**, **Open chat** (a `mailto:` link with the body prefilled per RFC 6068, `tg://user?id=` or `vk.com/im?sel=`), **I sent it myself** and **Skip**.
  - "Send all" appears only after safe mode is switched off, and it still asks once.

## Screenshots

These come from `experiments/reengage-spa-server.mjs`: a seeded store with a fake sender, driven with Playwright.

Safe mode on first open: Аня on Telegram, "ты" detected, so the informal text is prefilled.

![safe mode](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-31-5ccfae6dabce/docs/case-studies/issue-31/screenshots/reengage-safe-mode.png?raw=true)

After **Send**: the next contact (VK) used "вы", so the formal text is prefilled.

![formal after send](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-31-5ccfae6dabce/docs/case-studies/issue-31/screenshots/reengage-formal-after-send.png?raw=true)

A failed send shows an alert and stays on the same draft:

![send failed](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-31-5ccfae6dabce/docs/case-studies/issue-31/screenshots/reengage-send-failed.png?raw=true)

Safe mode off shows **Send all (n)**:

![batch](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-31-5ccfae6dabce/docs/case-studies/issue-31/screenshots/reengage-batch-mode.png?raw=true)

## How to reproduce

```bash
node experiments/reengage-spa-server.mjs   # http://127.0.0.1:4791 → Re-engage
node experiments/reengage-cli-roundtrip.mjs
meta-sovereign reengage --interactive      # against your own store
```

## Tests

| File | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `js/tests/address-form.test.js` | markers, false-positive collisions (выход, работы, в интернете, на сайте), owner weighting, tie / no evidence, zh / hi, user pattern rules |
| `js/tests/reengage.test.js` | dormant detection, chat kinds, owner detection, templates, open-chat links, cooldown records, safe vs. batch sessions |
| `js/tests/reengage-cli.test.js` | preview, interactive keys, batch with and without confirmation |
| `js/tests/reengage-server.test.js` | plan, `confirm-required`, 502 on failure, mark, batch-only run, 405 |
| `js/tests/reengage-web.test.js` | screen markup in all 4 locales, safe-mode switch, notices, offline send |

Local gates pass: `npm test` 551/551, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication`. The logs are in `docs/case-studies/issue-31/verification-logs/`.

## Documentation

- `docs/REQUIREMENTS*.md` section W (R-W1..R-W11), `docs/USER-GUIDE*.md` section 10 and `docs/SERVER-PARITY*.md` section 5a, each in en/ru/zh/hi.
- The case study in `docs/case-studies/issue-31/`: requirements mapping, solution plan, external research (RFC 6068, Telegram deep links, VK peer ids) and known limits.
- Changeset: `.changeset/issue-31-reengage.md` (minor).
- `docs/case-studies/issue-31/` previously held a case study about the *pipeline template's* issue 31. It moved unchanged to `docs/case-studies/pipeline-template-issue-31/`.

## Known limits

- `/api/reengage/*` exists only on the JS server; this is recorded in SERVER-PARITY. Without a server the screen still plans locally, and Copy / Open chat / I sent it myself work; only Send needs the server.
- Telegram exports identify people by numeric ids, so Open chat uses `tg://user?id=`, which does not prefill text. Telegram documents `t.me/<username>?text=` for usernames, which can be used once an importer records usernames.
- Address-form rules ship for ru/zh/hi. Other T–V languages (du/Sie, tu/vous) can be added as `pattern:*` links.
title: feat(crm): re-engage personal contacts silent for 90+ days with ты/вы detection and a safe one-by-one mode (#31)
